title: Annex B literal trap
blurb: A 16-case live edge and failure battery covering literal A/z/Z matching without u/v flags, character-class and quantifier SyntaxErrors, sticky lastIndex behavior, and \Z absorbing only one line break.
question: How do \A, \z, and \Z behave at grammar and flag boundaries—without u/v flags, inside character classes, under quantifiers, with sticky lastIndex, and before double line breaks?
result: Verified in Chrome 153 headless: 16/16 edge cases pass with --js-flags=--js-regexp-buffer-boundaries (7 pass and 9 report unsupported without the flag). Without u/v, /\Afoo/ matches 'Afoo' and /end\Z/ matches 'endZ'; /[\A]/u and /\z+/u throw SyntaxError; /end\Z/u rejects 'end\n\n'.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (default and --js-flags=--js-regexp-buffer-boundaries); not verified flag-free in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Omitting the u or v flag silently turns \A, \z, and \Z into Annex B identity escapes matching literal 'A', 'z', and 'Z' instead of throwing
friction.repro: Run /\Afoo/.test('Afoo') or /end\Z/.test('endZ') without the u or v flag; both return true and fail to match 'foo' or 'end\n'.
friction.browser: Chrome 153 (and all Annex B JavaScript engines)
friction.workaround: Always compile patterns using \A, \z, or \Z with the u or v flag, and lint against flagless buffer escapes.

friction.summary: The TC39 proposal README's /end\Z/ example omits the u flag and therefore matches literal 'endZ' rather than end-of-buffer
friction.repro: Evaluate /end\Z/.test('end\n') vs /end\Z/.test('endZ'); without the u flag it returns false for 'end\n' and true for 'endZ'.
friction.workaround: Add the u or v flag (/end\Z/u) whenever copying buffer-boundary examples into JavaScript.
